identity_evidence.quote: bilateral conjunctival manifestations in a 2-month-old domestic mixed-breed kitten

attribution_limitations: The abstract says that after 1 month of therapy the lesions disappeared, leaving the only sequelae as adhesion of the third eyelid to the palpebral conjunctiva. The case text reports clinical resolution 30 days after the topical lotion, remission after 4 months of treatment, and bilateral symblepharon plus eyelid fibrosis at the end of therapy.

Figure 5A text and caption describe the same time point differently: the text says the clinical response remained unsatisfactory 30 days after dose adjustment (Figure 5A), while the caption for panel A at 65 days reports significant reduction in lesion volume and exudate, less friable masses and onset of re-epithelialization.

The abstract lists a food supplement containing beta-glucans and says treatment began with oral itraconazole and topical adjuvant therapy, while the case text gives beta-glucans (Macrogard) only inside the compounded topical lotion introduced after the response to oral itraconazole remained unsatisfactory.

The text cites Figure 5C for the end-of-therapy symblepharon and eyelid fibrosis after a total of 4 months and 5 days of treatment, while the Figure 5C caption labels the panel 120 days. The findings agree; only the day count differs, and only by arithmetic.

The source says molecular methods would provide more robust species-level confirmation and are often not routinely available; no species-level result is reported and the organism is named only as Sporothrix spp.

The owner used gentamicin with dexamethasone eye drops and systemic corticosteroids while gentamicin sulfate drops had been instituted for 15 days; the source does not state whether the owner-given drops replaced or overlapped the prescribed gentamicin, or the start date of the owner-given medications.

claims.text: A male mixed-breed kitten, approximately 2 months old and weighing 300 g, rescued from the streets, was referred to a veterinary ophthalmology service after ocular alterations had been empirically treated as chronic bilateral conjunctivitis without response, using several eye drops and ointments per the caregiver. Examination showed intense bilateral conjunctival hyperemia, granulomatous appearance, follicles, chemosis, thick mucopurulent discharge and malnutrition, without cutaneous lesions.
